# Running Cursor AI Agents on a Headless Server

Cursor offers two fully headless paths for running AI coding agents without a desktop IDE — **Cursor CLI** (a local terminal agent) and **Cursor Cloud Agents** (background agents that run in remote VMs). The desktop IDE is only required if you want the full GUI experience; neither headless path needs it.

---

## Option 1 — Cursor CLI (recommended for headless servers)

Cursor CLI is a standalone `agent` binary that runs entirely in a terminal. It does not require an X server, display, or any desktop environment. It is the standard way to automate Cursor on a headless machine.

**Sources:** [Cursor CLI overview](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview.md), [installation](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/installation.md), [using](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using.md), [headless guide](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless.md), [authentication reference](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/authentication.md), [GitHub Actions](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/github-actions.md).

### Installation

```bash
# macOS, Linux, Windows (WSL)
curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash

# Windows (native PowerShell)
irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex
```

- The binary installs to `~/.local/bin/agent`. Add it to your PATH if it isn't already:
  ```bash
  # bash
  echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
  # zsh
  echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc && source ~/.zshrc
  ```
- Verify with `agent --version`.
- CLI **auto-updates** by default; you can force update with `agent update`.

### Authentication on a headless machine

There are two methods, and which you pick is dictated by the headless context:

**1. Browser-based login (interactive — needs a browser to complete once):**
```bash
agent login
```
On a true headless box this is awkward. Cursor supports the env var `NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1`, which prints the login URL instead of auto-opening a browser, so you can copy it to your laptop to complete the OAuth flow:
```bash
NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1 agent login
```
Useful commands: `agent status` (verify auth), `agent logout` (clear credentials). Credentials are stored locally after login, so subsequent invocations don't need a browser.

**2. API key (recommended for fully headless / CI / scripted use):**
- Generate a key at **Cursor Dashboard → API Keys** (`https://cursor.com/dashboard/api`).
- Provide it one of two ways:
  ```bash
  export CURSOR_API_KEY=your_api_key_here    # env var (recommended for automation)
  agent "implement user authentication"
  ```
  or:
  ```bash
  agent --api-key your_api_key_here "..."
  ```

The API key path is what you want on a headless server, in cron jobs, systemd services, Docker containers, CI runners, etc. Treat it like any other secret — put it in a secrets manager, not a config file.

### Basic usage

**Interactive REPL** (rarely useful on a headless box, but works over SSH/TTY):
```bash
agent
agent "refactor the auth module to use JWT tokens"
```

**Non-interactive / print mode — the headless sweet spot:**
```bash
# One-shot prompt with final answer to stdout
agent -p "find and fix performance issues" --model gpt-5

# Allow actual file edits (without --force, edits are only proposed)
agent -p --force "Refactor this code to use modern ES6+ syntax"

# Ask mode (read-only, no edits) for inspections
agent -p --mode=ask "summarize the public API of this repo"

# Plan mode for design-before-code
agent -p --plan "how would you add SSO to this app?"
```

**Output formats for scripts/CI:**
- `text` (default under `-p`) — clean final answer.
- `json` — structured result, easy to parse with `jq`.
- `stream-json` — message-level streaming; add `--stream-partial-output` for incremental text deltas. Useful for live progress UIs.

```bash
agent -p --force --output-format json "Add JSDoc comments to src/"
```

**Other useful flags/commands:**
- `agent ls` — list past chats.
- `agent resume` / `agent --continue` / `agent --resume <id>` — resume a session.
- `--worktree <name>` / `-w` — run the agent in a fresh Git worktree (`~/.cursor/worktrees/`) so your checkout stays clean.
- `--workspace <path>` — explicit repo root.
- `--api-key <key>` — inline key (alternative to env).
- `/sandbox` or `--sandbox enabled|disabled` — toggle command sandbox; you can also toggle network within it.
- ACP server for custom integrations: `agent acp` (stdio JSON-RPC).
- Cloud handoff from inside a session: prepend `&` to a message to push it to a Cloud Agent mid-conversation.

**Permission restrictions for production automation** — pair CI use with a permissions file so the agent can't go outside scope:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Read(**/*.md)", "Write(docs/**/*)", "Shell(grep)", "Shell(find)"],
    "deny":  ["Shell(git)", "Shell(gh)", "Write(.env*)", "Write(package.json)"]
  }
}
```

### Server requirements

A Linux/macOS machine with:
- A shell (bash/zsh) accessible over SSH.
- Outbound HTTPS to the Cursor API.
- `~/.local/bin` writable for the binary.
- For `--force`/`agent` shell calls: ability to run arbitrary commands (or restrict via permissions config).
- No display server / no GUI / no Electron.

The same install path works for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Cron, Docker, Kubernetes jobs, etc., as long as you can `curl` the install script and export an API key.

---

## Option 2 — Cursor Cloud Agents / Background Agents

These are the same thing — Cloud Agents used to be called "Background Agents". They run on **isolated VMs in the cloud**, not on your headless box at all. The server doesn't need to run any Cursor code itself; your server just has to be able to reach the Git host where the PR ends up.

**Sources:** [Cloud Agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent.md), [Background agents](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/background-agents.md), [Setup](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/setup.md), [Capabilities](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/capabilities.md), [Automations](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/automations.md).

### When to choose Cloud Agents over CLI

Use Cloud Agents when you want long-running, fully autonomous tasks that:
- Take minutes or hours.
- Need a full dev environment (clone repo, install deps, run tests).
- Should keep going after you log off.
- Can run in parallel — you can have many at once.
- Should produce merge-ready PRs with proof artifacts (screenshots, videos, logs).

Use CLI when you want short, scripted, deterministic automation on your own machine.

### How to start them (without any IDE)

You do **not** need the desktop IDE at all. Cursor Admin first connects your source control (GitHub Cloud/Enterprise Server, GitLab Cloud/Self-Hosted, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps). Then start agents from any of:

1. **Web**: [cursor.com/agents](https://cursor.com/agents).
2. **iOS**: Cursor iOS app.
3. **Android**: PWA installed from `cursor.com/agents` in Chrome.
4. **Desktop IDE**: select **Cloud** in the agent input dropdown (optional).
5. **Slack**: `@cursor` in a channel.
6. **GitHub / Bitbucket**: comment `@cursor` on a PR or issue.
7. **Linear**: `@cursor` command.
8. **Automations**: scheduled or event-triggered runs via the Automations UI.
9. **API**: programmatic kickoff.

You manage agents from the dashboard — view artifacts, take over the agent's remote desktop, follow up, share read-only links, etc.

### Requirements

- Paid Cursor plan (Pro/Business/Enterprise).
- An admin who has connected your GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket / Azure DevOps account.
- Read-write repo permissions for the agent's account.
- (Recommended) Secrets configured at `cursor.com/dashboard/cloud-agents`.
- (Recommended) An [environment](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/setup.md) defined via `.cursor/environment.json` or an agent-led setup — this controls installed deps, startup commands, network egress, snapshots. Builds prepare environments in the background for fast agent startup.
- (Enterprise) Network configuration: domain allow-lists, Tailscale, private connectivity for source control.

### Pricing

Cloud Agents are billed at **API pricing** for the chosen model. You'll set a spend limit on first use; the cursor.com dashboard shows cost per run.

---

## Is the desktop IDE required?

**No.** Neither headless path requires the desktop IDE.

| Path | Desktop IDE needed? | GUI/display needed? | Runs code where |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| Cursor CLI (`agent`) | No | No (terminal only) | Your headless server |
| Cloud Agents | No | No | Cursor's cloud VMs |
| Desktop IDE (GUI) | Yes — that's the whole point | Yes | Your local desktop |

Pick **CLI** for self-hosted scripting, CI/CD, cron jobs, SSH sessions on a VPS, in-container automation. Pick **Cloud Agents** for long-running autonomous work that should produce PRs and keep going unattended.

---

## Summary / Quick start for a headless server

```bash
# 1. Install
curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc
agent --version

# 2. Authenticate (pick one)
export CURSOR_API_KEY=sk-...                       # API key — best for headless
# — or —
NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1 agent login                      # browser flow, print URL to open elsewhere

# 3. Use it
agent -p "find and fix performance issues"          # one-shot, text output
agent -p --force "Add JSDoc to src/"                 # one-shot with file edits
agent -p --output-format json "Review this PR" | jq # structured output for scripts
agent --mode=ask "What does this service do?"       # read-only exploration
```

For unattended long-running work that should produce a PR, connect GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps under Integrations and run Cloud Agents from `cursor.com/agents` — no Cursor binary needed on the server at all.

Sources: [Cursor CLI overview](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview.md), [CLI installation](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/installation.md), [CLI using](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/using.md), [CLI headless guide](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/headless.md), [CLI authentication](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/authentication.md), [CLI GitHub Actions](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/github-actions.md), [CLI permissions](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions.md), [Cloud Agents](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent.md), [Background agents](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/background-agents.md), [Cloud agent setup](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/setup.md), [Automations](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/automations.md).
